title: Ex vivo assay to evaluate the efficacy of drugs targeting sphingolipids in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection of nasal epithelial cells
protocol: Start new BHK-21(G43) cell culture.
Seed BHK-21(G43) cells into T-75 flask in 10 mL medium (10% FBS).
Grow cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 in a standard tissue incubator.
Remove old culture medium from cells once they reach 75% confluence.
Add new culture medium containing 10−8 M mifepristone and incubate for 6 hours.
Remove the medium after 6 hours.
Add 8 mL DMEM containing diluted (1:1,000) VSV∗ΔG-FLuc stock to the cells.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Wash cells gently with PBS two to three times.
Add 20 mL DMEM supplemented with high glucose and 5% FCS plus 10−8 M mifepristone.
Incubate overnight (16–24 hours) at 37°C in a 5% CO2 environment.
Collect the supernatant once most cells are rounded and detached.
Centrifuge to pellet cellular debris for 10 minutes at 2,000 × g at 22°C.
Prepare 1 mL aliquots of the supernatant in cryo vials.
Flash-freeze samples and store at -80°C.
Seed HEK293T cells into 96-well plates (3 x 10^4 cells/well) one day prior to infection.
Grow cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 until they reach 75% confluence for infection.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions of VSV∗ΔG-FLuc stock by mixing 900 μL culture medium with 100 μL VSV∗ΔG-FLuc stock or previous dilution.
Inoculate cells with serially diluted VSV∗ΔG-FLuc in technical triplicates or quadruplicates.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour in a 5% CO2 environment.
Remove medium from cell cultures.
Wash cells gently with PBS, repeating 2–3 times.
Add 100 μL of fresh culture medium per well.
Incubate the plates for 16–24 hours at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Count eGFP-positive cells using a fluorescence microscope or automated reader.
Calculate the titer of VSV∗ΔG-FLuc stocks using the formula provided.
Start new CRL-2700 cell culture by seeding up to 10th passage cells at a density of 1 × 10^4 cells/mL in T-75 flasks with medium containing 10% FBS.
Grow cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 in an upright position tissue incubator.
Split the cells 1:4 when they reach a density of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL to obtain four T-75 flasks.
Continue cultivating until cell density reaches 1 × 10^6 cells/mL again.
Add 30 mL of FBS-free culture medium (final concentration = 2.5%) when the desired cell density is achieved.
Continue cultivation until the density reaches 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Collect all cultures (= 160 mL).
Add 240 mL of FBS-free culture medium (final FBS concentration = 1%).
Seed 40 mL of cell suspension into 10 × T-175 flasks.
Continue cultivation until the density reaches 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Collect all cultures (= 400 mL) and transfer into 50 mL sterile centrifugal tubes.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 600 × g to pellet cells.
Aliquot pelleted cells in MEM/DMEM + 10% FBS + 10% DMSO and freeze.
Collect supernatant in a separate tube.
Load supernatant on Vivaspin Protein Concentrator Columns (molecular weight cut-off: 30 kDa).
Centrifuge at 4,000 × g/4°C until the total volume is reduced to ∼40 mL (∼10-fold concentrated).
Aliquot concentrated supernatant in cryo vials.
Store samples at -20°C (or -80°C).
Remove culture supernatant from HEK293T cells.
Add 100 μL/well of VSV*ΔG-FLuc (VSV-G)/antibody mixtures.
Incubate for 16–24 h.
Check for eGFP-positive (infected) cells using a fluorescence microscope.
Start new HEK293T cell culture.
Seed low passage HEK293T cells into 6-well plates at 3 × 10^5 cells/well.
Grow cells for 24 h at 37°C with 5% CO2 in a standard tissue incubator.
Mix 6–8 μg of plasmid-DNA (pCG1-SARS-2-S or pCAGGS-VSV-G) per well and sterile ultrapure water to a final volume of 112.5 μL.
Add 12.5 μL of sterile-filtered CaCl2 (stock conc. 2.5 M) and mix thoroughly.
Add 125 μL of sterile-filtered 2× HBS buffer and vortex.
Incubate for 15 min at 22°C.
Mix the transfection complexes dropwise to the cells.
Incubate overnight (16–18 hours) at 37°C with 5% CO2 in a standard tissue incubator.
Remove supernatant and inoculate cells with 1 mL VSV∗ΔG-FLuc (or VSV-G as positive control), MOI = 3.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C and 5% CO2 in a standard tissue incubator.
Remove supernatant carefully and wash the cells 1–2 times with PBS.
Add fresh medium containing anti-VSV-G antibodies (except for cells transfected with VSV-G; add fresh medium without anti-VSV-G antibodies instead).
Incubate overnight (16–18 hours) at 37°C with 5% CO2 in a standard tissue incubator.
Collect supernatant and remove cellular debris by centrifugation at 2,000 × g for 10 minutes.
Transfer clarified supernatants into fresh tubes.
Use supernatants either directly for transduction of target cells or store supernatants at -80°C.
Transfer 1 mL prewarmed H/S buffer to each microtube, one tube per volunteer.
Insert the brush 1.5 to 2 cm into the nose and gently rotate it to collect epithelial cells.
Release cells directly from the brush into the H/S buffer in the microtube by rotating the brush carefully.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down once to mix the cells thoroughly.
Split the volume of each sample equally into identical aliquots.
Centrifuge cells at 22°C, 830 × g for 10 min to pellet them.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Directly after nasal cell isolation, human volunteers take amitriptyline orally (0.5 mg/kg).
Isolate nasal epithelial cells 1.5 h after medication intake, identical to previous steps.
Isolate nasal epithelial cells 24 h after medication intake, identical to previous steps.
Resuspend cells of two aliquots in 100 μL prewarmed MEM/10% FCS containing pp-VSV-SARS-CoV-2 spike (infected sample).
Transfer resuspended cells into one well of a 96-well plate each.
Incubate cells for 30 min at 37°C to determine Asm activity and ceramide amounts.
Incubate cells for 60 min at 37°C to determine infection rates.
Transfer cells into a micro tube.
Centrifuge cells.
Wash cells once with H/S buffer.
Discard supernatant.
Shock-freeze cells without buffer.
Store shock-frozen cells at -80°C.
Alternatively, resuspend cells in 100 μL fresh MEM/10% FCS.
Culture cells for 24 hours to allow eGFP expression.
Transfer cells into a micro tube the next day.
Spin down cells at 830 × g for 10 minutes.
Remove medium.
Resuspend cells in 20 μL H/S.
Pipette an aliquot of 10 μL onto a glass slide.
Cover with a cover slip.
Visualize cells on a fluorescence microscope.
Prepare a fresh 10 μM amitriptyline solution in 0.9% NaCl.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of the 10 μM amitriptyline solution and transfer into one well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate for 60 min at 37°C in an incubator.
Centrifuge the treated cells as specified.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL prewarmed MEM/10% FCS containing pp-VSV-SARS-CoV-2 spike.
Continue with step 44 of section Cellular infection with pp-VSV-CoV-2 spike.
Centrifuge freshly prepared cell samples and discard the supernatant.
Shock-frozen cell pellets should be quickly thawed at 37°C using a thermo shaker.
Place 270 μL pre-cooled Asm dilution buffer into a new micro tube for each sample to be analyzed.
Remove [14C]sphingomyelin from the freezer and pipette 0.1 μL [14C]sphingomyelin, corresponding to 0.05 μCi, for each sample into one new micro tube.
Dry the sphingomyelin resolved in organic solvent in a vacuum concentrator for 10 min (larger volumes may take longer).
Transfer frozen samples into a thermo shaker and thaw them quickly at 37°C.
Add 200 μL pre-cooled Asm lysis buffer to each sample and place samples on ice for 5 min.

Add 30 μL Asm assay buffer per original 0.1 μL to dried sphingomyelin (e.g., 20 samples means 630 μL assay buffer ([20+1]×30 μL)) and sonicate in a sonication bath for 10 min to promote micelle formation.
Add 30 μL of lysed sample to pre-pipetted Asm dilution buffer to dilute NP40 concentration to 0.2% (final volume, Vend = 300 μL).
Add 30 μL of sonicated [14C]sphingomyelin (in Asm assay buffer) to each sample (Vend = 330 μL).
Incubate samples on a thermo shaker prewarmed to 37°C for 30 - 60 min at 300 rpm horizontal shaking and 37°C.
Terminate enzymatic reaction by adding 800 μL of freshly mixed lipid extraction mixture (CHCl3:CH3OH, 2:1, v/v) to each sample.
Vortex each sample for 30 s.
Centrifuge samples at maximum speed in a micro centrifuge for 5 min to separate hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases.
Pipette 4 mL scintillation fluid into a scintillation vial for each sample.
Take an aliquot of the upper phase by pipetting twice 125 μL from prepared samples very carefully without mixing the two phases or taking anything from the lower or intermediate phase.
Add 20 μL of [14C]sphingomyelin in Asm assay buffer to 4 mL scintillation liquid for positive control preparation.
Prepare negative control by adding scintillation fluid only, without a sample.
Vortex each scintillation vial for 10 s and wait for 10 min before analyzing them in a scintillation counter.
Convert the counts of each sample using the specific activity of [14C]sphingomyelin into moles.
Consider the time of assay and amount of protein used to calculate specific Asm activity (mol/mg/h).
Determine protein concentration with a commercial kit compared to a calibration series.
Use the remaining lysed sample in Asm lysis buffer for ceramide determination optionally.
Shock-freeze or store samples at -80°C if they are not immediately used for quantitative ceramide determination.
Centrifuge freshly prepared cell samples and discard the supernatant.
Shock-freeze cell pellets and store at -80°C until use for ceramide assay.
Quickly thaw shock-frozen cell pellets at 37°C using a thermo shaker.
Prepare a TLC chamber with 100 mL of TLC running buffer consisting of CHCl3:C3H6O:CH3OH:C2H4O2:H2O (50:20:15:10:5; v/v/v/v/v).
Resuspend each sample in 200 μL H2O or use the rest of hydrophilic sample from Asm activity assay.
Extract lipids by adding 600 μL lipid extraction mixture consisting of CHCl3:CH3OH:1 N HCl (100:100:1; v/v/v) and vortex for 10 s.
Use 50, 100, 250, and 500 pmol of C16 and C24 ceramide for standards.
Centrifuge samples for 5 min at 22°C and maximum speed.
Transfer 180 μL of the lower phase into a new 2 mL micro tube and dry the samples in a vacuum concentrator.
Thaw [32P]γATP at 22°C until it is ready (approximately 1 hour).
Re-dissolve dried samples in 20 μL detergent solution.
Add 70 μL of master mix to each sample to start the kinase reaction.
Incubate for 60 min at 22°C with shaking on a horizontal mixer (350 rpm).
Stop the kinase reaction by adding 1 mL lipid extraction mixture and vortexing for 10 s.
Add 170 μL complete salt solution and vortex for 10 s.
Add 30 μL of 100 mM EDTA solution to promote phase separation and vortex once again.
Centrifuge the samples at 22°C for 5 min at maximum speed.
Transfer 2 times 170 μL of the lower phase into a new 1.5 mL micro tube and dry the samples in a vacuum concentrator.
Re-dissolve dried samples in 20 μL freshly prepared CHCl3:CH3OH (1:1; v/v).
Spot the dissolved samples in 3–4 μL steps onto a thin-layer chromatography plate.
Place a sheet of squared paper at the bottom of the TLC plate for orientation of sample application points.
Choose an appropriate distance between spotting dots on the TLC plate.
Apply the horizontal line of the application points to be 1 to 1.5 cm from the lower edge of the plate.
Use CHCl3:C3H6O:CH3OH:C2H4O2:H2O (50:20:15:10:5; v/v/v/v/v) as running buffer for chromatography.
Run samples until the solvent front reaches the end of the TLC plate.
Analyze TLC plates with an appropriate imager.
Quantify ceramide spots in comparison to standard C16 and C24 ceramide series using software.
